Chords in Every Key: Transposition Chart

Every major key uses the same pattern of seven chords. Once you know the pattern, you can transpose any song by reading across a table — or by letting the app do it.

The chord pattern of a major key

Build a triad on each note of a major scale and you get seven chords. Their qualities always follow the same order:

DegreeQualityIn CRole
ImajorCHome. Songs usually start and end here.
IImminorDmOften leads to V.
IIImminorEmA softer substitute for I or V.
IVmajorFMoves away from home.
Vmajor (often V7)GTension that pulls back to I.
VImminorAmThe relative minor: the "sad" home.
VIIdimdiminishedBdimRare in pop; often played as V7 instead.

Roman numerals describe a chord by its position in the key, so "I–V–VIm–IV" means the same progression in any key.

Chords are spelled from each key's scale, so the key of F# has E#dim (the same pitch as Fdim). Db and F# are written the usual way; their twins C# and Gb use the same pitches.

Transpose with the chart

To move a song from one key to another, find each chord in the row of the old key, then read the chord in the same column of the new key.

Example: a song in G uses G, Em, C, and D (I, VIm, IV, V). In the key of Bb, the same columns give Bb, Gm, Eb, and F.

Doing this by hand gets slow with long songs and chords such as D7sus4 or F#m7-5. Chord Transposer moves every chord in the chart in one step and keeps the spacing between chords and lyrics. For flat keys such as Bb, set #/♭ to Prefer b so the chords come out as Bb and Eb rather than A# and D#.

How many semitones between two keys?

The app transposes by semitones. Rows are the original key and columns are the new key: find the original key in the left column and the new key at the top; the number is the value to choose in Transpose. The table shows the smaller move (up to 6 semitones). Moving the other way also works: +5 and -7 give the same chords, an octave apart.

For example, G → Bb is +3, and E → C is -4.

Singers often move a key by just one or two semitones. Try a small change first, then sing a line or two before going further.

Sevenths, slash chords, and other chords

  • Extensions stay the same. Only the letter name (the root) moves: Cmaj7 +2 is Dmaj7, and G7sus4 +2 is A7sus4.
  • Slash chords move both notes. C/E +2 is D/F#.
  • Chords outside the key (borrowed chords such as Bb in the key of C) move by the same number of semitones as everything else.
